cards.text: Amos, a sheepherder from Tekoa, has been bringing the LORD's judgment on nation after nation: Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab and even Judah (Amos 1:1-2:5). Now the LORD says, "For three transgressions of Israel, even four, I will not revoke My judgment." I bet Israel was nodding along right up until they heard their OWN name.

cards.question: The LORD's first charge is that Israel sells the righteous for silver. What do they sell the needy for?

cards.text: A pair of SANDALS. Friend, Mother Miller paid a quarter for me out of a bakery's last bin, and even I'd be insulted by that price.

cards.question: The LORD says Israel tramples on the heads of the poor as on the dust of the earth. What do they do to the needy who are in their way?

cards.text: Then the LORD names another sin. A man and his father have relations with the same girl.

cards.question: The LORD says that sin between a man, his father and the same girl profanes His holy name.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to their worship. They lie down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge.

cards.question: Israel also drinks wine obtained through fines. Where do they drink it?

answers.text: In the house of their God
In the palace of the king
At the gate of the city

cards.text: Then the LORD brings up the Amorite, who was as tall as the cedars and as strong as the oaks. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper, and some days I LOSE a wrestling match with an oven mitt.

cards.question: Israel beat the Amorite because Israel's men were even taller and stronger.

cards.text: Not even close. The LORD says He destroyed the Amorite, fruit above and roots below, and He brought Israel up from the land of Egypt.

cards.question: After Egypt, the LORD led Israel ___ years in the wilderness, so they could take possession of the land of the Amorite.

cards.text: He also raised up prophets from their sons and Nazirites from their young men. Then the LORD asks, "Is this not true, O children of Israel?"

cards.question: Israel honors the prophets the LORD raised up and lets them prophesy.
And the Nazirites the LORD raised up? Israel made them drink ___.

cards.text: Ordering the prophets to stop prophesying is like yanking the battery out of a smoke detector, and the dead batteries I shared that drawer with would be OFFENDED. Then the LORD says, "Behold, I am about to crush you in your place as with a cart full of grain."

cards.question: Israel has swift runners, strong men and mighty warriors. When the LORD crushes them, who will save himself?
On that day, the archer, the fleet of foot and the horseman will at least get away.
What does the LORD say even the bravest of mighty men will do on that day?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "For three transgressions of Israel, even four, I will not revoke My judgment.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card uses facts from outside the passage: Amos as a sheepherder from Tekoa, and the list of nations judged before Israel. It cites them in the text as (Amos 1:1-2:5), but its verses field is only Amos 2:6. The docs require outside facts to carry their reference. They also say a story card cites every verse it uses. They don't say whether outside verses belong in the card's verses field or only in the text.
findings.question: When a story card uses context from outside the passage, should its verses field include those outside verses, such as Amos 1:1-2:6, or stay inside the passage with the outside reference given only in the text?

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the answer to card 2 (a pair of SANDALS) and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward, so it works as a recap or reaction card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. Papa Dorin was bought for a quarter, and a pair of sandals sounds like more than that, so it's unclear why he would be insulted by the sandals price. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The question frames this as one of the LORD's charges right after trampling the poor. The wrong answers are kind acts (give them shelter, hire them for work), so the setup rules them out and the right answer stands out by tone.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The answers don't share a tone. The right answer is a harsh act and both wrong answers are kind acts, so the right answer is obvious.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Card 5 says "the LORD names another sin," and card 6 says "that sin." The passage calls these transgressions (Amos 2:6) and says the act profanes His holy name. It doesn't use the word sin.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Then the LORD turns to their worship" points straight to the answer of card 8 (in the house of their God) and rules out the palace and the city gate.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The Amorite appears for the first time with no simple word on who he is. He stands for a people who lived in the land before Israel took it.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke blends two images: a smoke detector battery being pulled, and the drawer's dead batteries being offended. It's unclear why the drawer batteries would be offended, so the punchline doesn't click.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The right answer "Not even the mighty" has a different form from the two wrong answers, which both start with "Only the." It's also the only answer that doesn't name someone who saves himself, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
